key_insight: An AI model’s public name can stay the same even as the model or its surrounding system changes. Meaningful versioning would make those changes identifiable, supporting reproducible research and regulatory oversight.
problem_solved: Unchanged public identifiers can hide updates to AI models and system integrations, making it difficult to track which version was evaluated, reproduce results, or maintain effective oversight.
method: Identify the transparency gap created when AI providers update models or integrations without changing public identifiers.
Argue for meaningful versioning that distinguishes changes relevant to researchers and regulators.
Frame versioning as an accountability practice rather than presenting a new model or experimental technique.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, meaningful versioning could make evaluations easier to reproduce and help clarify which system produced a result. It could also strengthen change tracking and regulatory accountability.
visual_elements: Before-and-after diagram: one unchanged AI name masking two different system versions.
Timeline showing model and integration updates alongside corresponding version identifiers.
Layered system graphic separating the AI model from its surrounding integrations.
Linked icons for version identification, reproducibility, and regulatory oversight.
paper_authors: Vasilios Mavroudis, Dan Ristea, Lauritz Morlock, Carlos Mougan
